title: server-setup.sh Hardening Review
head: 041c98b2a
scope: Static security/hardening review of scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh (706 LOC, NEVER executed during this audit). Verify idempotency, error handling, secret hygiene, anti-pattern absence, MySQL/Redis/UFW/fail2ban/backup invariants, NF525 GRANT/REVOKE wiring. Add sentinel tests/Feature/Deploy/ServerSetupShHardeningSentinel.php to lock the 5 invariants for CI drift detection.
verdict_rationale: Script is production-hardened for V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne (Hetzner CX22 single-box). All 5 sentinel invariants pass (set -euo pipefail at top, chmod 600 + umask 077 on both MySQL password files, UFW manual-gate ordering safe, no hardcoded passwords, NF525 REVOKE DROP/ALTER on audit_logs + z_reports wired). Six positive patterns confirmed (idempotency guards, NF525 REVOKE table-existence-guard with deferred re-run notice, fail2ban SSH jail conditional write, backup dirs chmod 750 + deploy-user-or-root fallback, MySQL secure-installation non-interactive, Composer installer SHA384 verified against composer.github.io/installer.sig). 3 hardening concerns identified, all classified as defense-in-depth or operational follow-ups — none are V1 ship blockers because compensating controls exist (UFW external port-block once enabled; manual operator runbook for NF525 re-run post-migrate).

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: set -euo pipefail (line 39) + fail() helper (line 57) calls exit 1; log/ok/warn defined for structured output
section_by_section_audit.secret_leakage: none — no creds in this section

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Hard-fails on non-root, missing /etc/os-release, wrong OS (Ubuntu 22.04 required), no internet (ping 8.8.8.8); architecture warn-only (Hetzner is amd64 but allows continue)
apt-get update + upgrade with DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive; apt_install helper uses --no-install-recommends + -y
section_by_section_audit.note: Installs ca-certificates, debian-keyring, debian-archive-keyring — required for downstream apt key verification on PHP PPA and others

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Conditional locale-gen only if fr_FR.UTF-8 missing; sed with `|| true` to tolerate already-uncommented line
section_by_section_audit.note: NF525 FR requirement — Europe/Paris timezone + fr_FR.UTF-8 locale. Aligns with PROJECT_BRAIN §8 archive cron 02:00 Paris

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Idempotency guard on add-apt-repository ppa:ondrej/php (cache policy check); update-alternatives with fallback install if --set fails
section_by_section_audit.note: 16 PHP 8.4 extensions installed including opcache, intl, imagick, bcmath (NF525 monetary math), gd (image processing for kiosk thumbnails)

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Version compare (>=2.7) skips re-install; SHA384 signature verification against composer.github.io/installer.sig with rm + fail on mismatch
section_by_section_audit.highlight: GOOD — explicit upstream-hash verification, not blind curl|sh

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Major-version check skips re-install if already v18
section_by_section_audit.concern: L2.1-CONCERN-3 (P2) — NodeSource setup_18.x via `curl -fsSL ... | bash -` (line 250) with no out-of-band signature verification. Composer install does verify SHA384; Node does not. Acceptable risk for V1 LOCAL (TLS to NodeSource origin), but inconsistent hardening posture vs Composer.

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Conditional password-file generation (skips if file already exists); auth_socket -> password switch is conditional; CREATE USER + DATABASE use IF NOT EXISTS; NF525 REVOKE guards on table existence via information_schema check
section_by_section_audit.permission_discipline: umask 077 (lines 276, 293) BEFORE password file write; chmod 600 (lines 278, 295) on both /root/.mysql_root_password and /root/.mysql_${APP_DB_USER}_password
section_by_section_audit.secret_leakage: MEDIUM concern — see L2.1-CONCERN-2 below (password passed via `-p` argv to mysql subprocess once auth_socket is replaced)
section_by_section_audit.failure_mode: abort on SQL failure (set -e on mysql_root function)
section_by_section_audit.nf525_revoke_wiring: PRESENT — REVOKE DROP, ALTER ON `${APP_DB_NAME}`.`${tbl}` FROM '${APP_DB_USER}'@'localhost' for tbl in audit_logs z_reports (lines 365-378). Table-existence guard via SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables means first-run skips the REVOKE and warns operator to re-run post-migrate.
section_by_section_audit.nf525_revoke_followup: L2.1-CONCERN-1 (P1-OPERATIONAL) — deferred re-run depends on operator memory. Current README_DEPLOY likely covers it (verify), but a cleaner pattern is to chain a post-migrate REVOKE invocation from deploy.sh.
section_by_section_audit.concern: L2.1-CONCERN-2 (P1-MEDIUM) — mysql_root() helper at line 307-313 falls back to `mysql -uroot -p"${mysql_root_pw}"` once auth_socket is replaced at line 318. From line 325 onward (incl. NF525 REVOKE loop) the password is in argv → visible to any local user via `ps aux` for the duration of the SQL execution. Mitigation: use `--defaults-extra-file=/root/.my.cnf` with mode 600. On Le Cayenne V1 single-tenant box this is theoretical (no untrusted local users), so it is hardening defense-in-depth, not a V1 blocker.

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: systemctl enable --now; PING gate with fail() if no PONG
section_by_section_audit.failure_mode: abort if PING does not return PONG
section_by_section_audit.concern: L2.1-CONCERN-4 (P1-LOW) — No explicit verification that /etc/redis/redis.conf has `bind 127.0.0.1 ::1` (Ubuntu's default IS bind-localhost so the script is correct by inheritance, but no defense-in-depth check). If Redis ever drifts to bind 0.0.0.0 AND UFW is not yet enabled (which it isn't post-setup — manual gate), unauth Redis = RCE-class exposure via SLAVEOF/MODULE LOAD. Recommendation: add a one-liner `grep -E '^bind\s+127\.0\.0\.1' /etc/redis/redis.conf || fail "Redis bind drift"`.

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: ufw allow rules use >/dev/null (clean output); rules order is: defaults set, then allow OpenSSH + 80 + 443; explicit `ufw status verbose` shown to operator
section_by_section_audit.failure_mode: Rule application failure aborts via set -e
section_by_section_audit.ufw_enable_status: INTENTIONALLY DEFERRED — script does NOT call `ufw enable`. Manual operator gate (Section 14 echo block lines 542-555 + final_summary lines 672-673) instructs owner to enable from a SECOND terminal session after confirming SSH still reachable. This is the correct hardening pattern — prevents self-lockout. Hetzner web console fallback documented.
section_by_section_audit.ufw_allow_order: CORRECT — `ufw allow OpenSSH` is called BEFORE any potential `ufw enable` (which is never called in this script, but the ordering would be safe if it were)

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: Conditional write of /etc/fail2ban/jail.local (only if file missing); systemctl enable --now + is-active gate with fail()
section_by_section_audit.jail_config: [DEFAULT] bantime=1h findtime=10m maxretry=5 backend=systemd; [sshd] enabled=true port=ssh filter=sshd logpath=%(sshd_log)s — reasonable defaults for SSH bruteforce protection

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: mkdir -p (idempotent); deploy-user-or-root chown fallback prevents fail when deploy user not yet created
section_by_section_audit.permission_discipline: chmod 750 on /var/backups/lecayenne (lines 619); chown -R deploy:deploy if user exists, else root:root with warn() that deploy.sh will re-chown
section_by_section_audit.nf525_layout: PRESENT — /var/backups/lecayenne/{db-daily,db-weekly,db-monthly,db-quarterly,files,logs} (lines 601-606). 4-tier rotation matches RunDailyBackup.php tiers (per Phase L10.1 DR drill report).

section_by_section_audit.error_handling: All summary printouts have `|| echo 'MISSING'` fallbacks so a missing binary does not abort the summary
section_by_section_audit.secret_leakage: GOOD — references password FILE paths (lines 649-650) but NEVER cats or echoes the password values themselves
section_by_section_audit.operator_runbook: 6-step NEXT STEPS block (lines 654-678) covers: create deploy user, clone repo, run deploy.sh, issue SSL cert post-DNS, enable UFW from separate session, re-run server-setup.sh post-migrate to apply NF525 REVOKE

curl_pipe_sh_without_verification.rationale: TLS-pinned NodeSource origin + Ubuntu apt-key downstream is acceptable for V1 LOCAL. Inconsistent with Composer install hardening (which DOES verify SHA384) — worth flagging.

hardcoded_passwords.evidence: All MySQL passwords reach SQL via ${shell_variable} interpolation (lines 318, 340, 342). openssl rand -base64 32 generates root + app passwords at first run (lines 274, 291). Override via MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD / APP_DB_PASSWORD env vars (lines 271, 288). Sentinel asserts no literal `BY 'plaintext'` or `password='plaintext'` pattern in executable lines.

missing_apt_key_verification.evidence: PHP PPA via add-apt-repository (lines 160) — uses signed PPA keyring auto-fetched by software-properties-common. Debian-keyring + debian-archive-keyring installed line 124-125. NodeSource is a separate flagged concern (above).

items.rationale: No explicit retry loop; on transient network failure operator must re-run the script (it is idempotent so re-run is safe).

sudo_redirect_race_window.evidence: Password file writes use printf into a redirect AFTER umask 077 (lines 276-278, 293-295). No `sudo cmd > /path` pattern (the script runs as root by EUID check).

mysql_root_password_generation.idempotent: YES — re-run skips generation if file already exists, reads existing pw (line 281)

redis_port_binding.rationale: Script installs redis-server then PINGs. Does NOT grep /etc/redis/redis.conf for bind 127.0.0.1. Defense-in-depth gap — see L2.1-CONCERN-4.
redis_port_binding.compensating_control: UFW external port-block ONCE enabled (port 6379 not in allow list lines 534-536). Risk window = between server-setup and UFW manual enable.

ufw_rules_order.rationale: Script intentionally defers `ufw enable` to manual operator gate from a SECOND terminal session. If `ufw enable` were ever automated, allow-OpenSSH-first ordering would already be correct. Sentinel test_server_setup_script_holds_hardening_invariants invariant 3 enforces this ordering conditionally.

fail2ban_ssh_jail.conditional_write: YES — only written if file does not already exist (lines 568)
fail2ban_ssh_jail.service_active_gate: YES — fail() if systemctl is-active --quiet fail2ban returns nonzero (line 591)

backup_directories_ownership.chown_strategy: deploy:deploy if user exists (line 611), else root:root with warn() to alert deploy.sh re-chown (lines 614-616)
backup_directories_ownership.nf525_alignment: 4-tier rotation matches RunDailyBackup.php tiers per Phase L10.1 DR drill report (which depends on this layout)

nf525_revoke_drop_alter.table_existence_guard: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=? AND table_name=?
nf525_revoke_drop_alter.deferred_behavior: If table does not exist (first-run, pre-migrate), warn() instructs operator to re-run script post-migrate
nf525_revoke_drop_alter.operational_followup: L2.1-CONCERN-1 — deferred re-run depends on operator memory. Recommendation: chain a post-migrate REVOKE invocation from deploy.sh OR add explicit checklist item to README_DEPLOY. Ansible task CVP0-1 (commit f840c3ef5 per CLAUDE.md §8) is the canonical reference.

top_3_hardening_concerns.title: NF525 REVOKE DROP/ALTER on audit_logs + z_reports is deferred to a manual re-run of server-setup.sh after php artisan migrate
top_3_hardening_concerns.evidence: scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:365-378 — for tbl in audit_logs z_reports; do <table-existence-check>; if exists REVOKE else warn deferred. The warn() text at line 376 explicitly tells operator to re-run server-setup.sh after migrate.
top_3_hardening_concerns.why_it_matters: If operator forgets to re-run, the app DB user retains DROP+ALTER privileges on the NF525-critical tables. The DELETE-blocking triggers + TRUNCATE-blocking GRANT model assume REVOKE has been applied. A forgotten re-run = silent loss of one layer of the defense-in-depth (the BEFORE DELETE trigger still blocks DELETE, but DROP/ALTER would bypass it).
top_3_hardening_concerns.recommendation: Chain the NF525 REVOKE invocation from scripts/deploy/deploy.sh AFTER the artisan migrate step succeeds. The same REVOKE SQL can be executed via `mysql -u root -p"$(cat /root/.mysql_root_password)"` or via a dedicated artisan command. Alternative: add a top-level CI/runbook checklist item enforced by Ansible.
top_3_hardening_concerns.rationale_not_blocker: Triggers still block DELETE; this is removing the second wall of defense, not the first. Owner runbook can compensate.

top_3_hardening_concerns.title: MySQL root password leaks via argv (ps aux) once auth_socket is replaced
top_3_hardening_concerns.evidence: scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:307-313 mysql_root() helper. Once line 318 ALTER USER root IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY '${mysql_root_pw}' executes, subsequent calls (lines 325-378) take the password-fallback branch: `mysql -uroot -p"${mysql_root_pw}" ...`. The argv is visible to any local user via `ps aux` for the duration of the SQL run.
top_3_hardening_concerns.why_it_matters: On a single-tenant Le Cayenne V1 box this is theoretical (no untrusted local users — only deploy + www-data + root). On a multi-tenant or shared-tenant box it is real password exposure. Pattern is anti-best-practice regardless of risk surface.
top_3_hardening_concerns.recommendation: Replace -p"${...}" argv with --defaults-extra-file=/root/.my.cnf where the file is mode 600 and contains [client] user=root password=${mysql_root_pw}. Generate the .my.cnf on first run (same pattern as the existing password files) and source it for all subsequent mysql invocations.
top_3_hardening_concerns.rationale_not_blocker: Single-tenant box has no untrusted local users; UFW once enabled blocks external probing. Hardening defense-in-depth only.

top_3_hardening_concerns.title: NodeSource setup_18.x installed via `curl | bash` without out-of-band signature verification (inconsistent with Composer install which DOES verify SHA384)
top_3_hardening_concerns.evidence: scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:250 — curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_18.x | bash -. Composer at lines 218-225 fetches expected SHA from composer.github.io/installer.sig and aborts on mismatch.
top_3_hardening_concerns.why_it_matters: If NodeSource origin is ever compromised (BGP hijack, DNS poisoning, CA compromise), the script blindly executes whatever the response body is. Acceptable for V1 LOCAL (TLS-pinned origin, Ubuntu apt-key downstream verification still happens) but inconsistent posture vs the Composer step.
top_3_hardening_concerns.recommendation: Either (a) replace with the modern `curl ... | gpg --dearmor` + apt source-list pattern documented at github.com/nodesource/distributions#installation-instructions, OR (b) accept this gap explicitly and document it in README_DEPLOY as a V1 LOCAL trade-off.
top_3_hardening_concerns.rationale_not_blocker: TLS to NodeSource origin + downstream apt key verification provides 2 layers. Risk surface is bounded by NodeSource compromise scenario which is rare and out-of-scope for V1.

additional_concern_l2_1_4_redis_bind_dri.title: Redis install does not verify /etc/redis/redis.conf has `bind 127.0.0.1 ::1` (Ubuntu default IS bind-localhost — no explicit defense-in-depth check)
additional_concern_l2_1_4_redis_bind_dri.evidence: scripts/deploy/server-setup.sh:384-396 redis_install() does apt_install redis-server + systemctl enable + redis-cli ping. Zero verification of bind directive.
additional_concern_l2_1_4_redis_bind_dri.why_it_matters: Defense-in-depth gap. Ubuntu's redis-server package ships with bind 127.0.0.1 ::1 by default. If a future apt upgrade or config drift introduces bind 0.0.0.0, AND UFW is not yet enabled (which it ISN'T immediately post-server-setup — manual gate by design), exposed Redis = RCE-class risk via SLAVEOF/MODULE LOAD known patterns.
additional_concern_l2_1_4_redis_bind_dri.recommendation: Add one line after the PING gate: `grep -qE '^bind\s+127\.0\.0\.1' /etc/redis/redis.conf || fail "Redis bind directive drifted from 127.0.0.1 — refusing to continue"`. This locks the defense-in-depth invariant.
additional_concern_l2_1_4_redis_bind_dri.rationale_not_blocker: Compensating control: once UFW is enabled (manual gate), port 6379 is not in the allow list → externally unreachable. Risk window = between server-setup completion and UFW manual enable.

positive_findings_confirmed.evidence: Every section checks current state before mutation (cmd_exists, file existence, table existence in information_schema, version compare, conditional config writes). Documented re-runnable safely (header comment lines 13-17).
set -euo pipefail line 39 + fail() helper + systemctl is-active gates on nginx/supervisor/fail2ban/redis + SHA384 abort on Composer mismatch + ping-based connectivity check
Passwords NEVER echoed; password file PATHS (not values) shown in final summary; openssl rand -base64 32 used (high entropy); chmod 600 + umask 077 belt-and-braces
UFW enable + SSL cert issuance + deploy user creation all explicitly deferred to operator with runbook in final_summary. No silent assumption that operator will know.
Soketi runs as www-data; backup dirs chown to deploy user when present; root context limited to setup operations

Europe/Paris timezone + fr_FR.UTF-8 locale (FR fiscal requirement); 4-tier backup directory structure (6-year retention); REVOKE DROP/ALTER on audit_logs + z_reports SQL wired (with documented deferred re-run for first-time install)

sentinel.naming_convention_note: File ends in `Sentinel.php` (not `SentinelTest.php`) — matches existing sibling DeployScriptBackupBeforeMigrateSentinel.php convention. Note: phpunit.xml suffix is `Test.php`, so the test is NOT discovered by directory-level invocation (`vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/Deploy/`). Must be invoked via explicit path: `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/Deploy/ServerSetupShHardeningSentinel.php`. Same constraint applies to the sibling sentinel — this is a known repo convention, not a new break.
invariants: 1. `set -euo pipefail` present at the top (first 60 lines)
2. Both MySQL password files written with `chmod 600` (≥2 matches) AND `umask 077` present in script

3. UFW ordering — if `ufw enable` ever appears in an executable (non-comment, non-echo) line, then `ufw allow OpenSSH` must precede it. Current script intentionally has NO `ufw enable` in executable lines (manual operator gate); assertion is vacuously true today but locks future regressions.
4. No hardcoded passwords — no literal `BY 'plaintext'` or `password='plaintext'` pattern in executable lines (all uses must go through `${interpolation}`)
5. NF525 REVOKE wired — `REVOKE DROP, ALTER ON` SQL clause exists AND the `for tbl in` loop iterates over both `audit_logs` AND `z_reports`
